title: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin for metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
context_label: Metastatic soft tissue sarcoma: the separate sarcoma indication of shared regimen 00205

purpose: Treatment aims to control metastatic sarcoma and help symptoms. A specialist considers tumour subtype, previous treatment, heart risk and your priorities; benefit is uncertain for an individual.
schedule_label: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² on day 1 every 28 days
schedule_summary: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² is given on day 1 every 28 days. National Cancer Control Programme describes typically 6 cycles or continuation until progression or unacceptable toxicity; the team confirms duration and review points.
administration_text: The pharmacy prepares only the pegylated liposomal formulation in glucose 5%; trained staff administer it without an in-line filter. National Cancer Control Programme specifies a first infusion rate of 1 mg/min and later 60-minute infusions if tolerated; a previous reaction requires a supervised modified sequence. The total visit includes blood tests, review, observation and line care.

agents.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Delivers doxorubicin in coated fat particles
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin damages the genetic material, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). In this formulation it is carried in tiny coated fat particles called liposomes, changing its distribution and side-effect pattern. It remains capable of causing heart injury and cannot be substituted for other doxorubicin formulations.
agents.watch: Report painful palms or soles, mouth ulcers and persistent oral lesions early. Report fever or new breathlessness urgently, and tell staff immediately about chest or throat tightness during an infusion.
risks: Painful red or blistered palms and soles (hand–foot syndrome), sometimes severe enough to limit everyday activities
Mouth soreness or ulcers that can impair eating and drinking; persistent mouth lesions require assessment
Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding; fatigue, nausea and bowel effects
Infusion reactions, sometimes serious; line leakage can damage tissue
Heart damage, including delayed injury; previous anthracycline exposure and cardiac disease matter
Lung inflammation; rare later blood cancers or oral cancers; fertility and pregnancy harm
visual: Mouth, skin, blood and heart checks

anatomy: Painful ulcers can limit eating and drinking. Report early and have persistent mouth lesions examined.
Heart injury remains possible with liposomal treatment. Report breathlessness, swelling, chest pain or palpitations.
Blood tests detect liver effects. Yellow eyes, dark urine or new significant upper abdominal pain needs prompt assessment.
New cough or breathlessness needs urgent review. Tell staff immediately about chest or throat tightness during infusion.
Low counts can cause infection, anaemia or bleeding. Fever, shaking chills or sudden illness needs immediate oncology contact.
Report persistent diarrhoea or constipation, severe pain, abdominal swelling or inability to drink.
Report painful redness, swelling or blisters on palms or soles early. Avoid heat and tight pressure after treatment.
Fatigue may continue between visits. Discuss fertility preservation and pregnancy precautions before treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check infection, anaemia and bleeding risks.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle. The 20 mg/m² and 50 mg/m² regimens have different source count decisions; additional checks follow symptoms and prior results.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify organ problems and review safe drug handling.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; repeat sooner when indicated by symptoms or abnormal results.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart function and cumulative exposure
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess cardiac risk despite the liposomal formulation.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Electrocardiogram (heart tracing) and heart pumping assessment at baseline; regular heart tracings during treatment and further pumping tests as indicated. Measure left ventricular ejection fraction, the heart pumping measurement, before each further dose taking lifetime anthracycline exposure above 450 mg/m². This threshold does not itself mean automatic treatment stopping.

monitoring_test_details.label: Mouth, palms and soles
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify painful ulcers or hand–foot inflammation before they become disabling.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Assess before each cycle and report symptoms between visits. Tell the team the worst symptoms and when they occurred; the team records their severity and any treatment delay.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour response, symptoms and function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from safety blood tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: The specialist sets scan and clinical-review timing for the tumour type, treatment aim and symptoms.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Confirm the exact pegylated liposomal product and all previous anthracycline doses. Report heart symptoms, mouth ulcers and painful hands or feet before the visit. Review interacting medicines, pregnancy precautions and any prior infusion reaction.  National Cancer Control Programme classifies this as low nausea/vomiting risk and lists no usual premedication. Follow individual anti-sickness and mouth-care advice. For 4–7 days after treatment, avoid excessive heat, friction and tight pressure on hands or feet; cooling measures and any skin treatment follow the local plan. Do not start routine vitamin or steroid hand–foot prophylaxis yourself.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and obtain written contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine, including how long precautions continue after the last dose. Do not assume all drugs have the same waiting period. Contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible. Current European product information specifies effective contraception for women during treatment and for 8 months afterwards, and for men with partners who could become pregnant during treatment and for 6 months afterwards. Stop breastfeeding before treatment. Pregnancy requires a specialist benefit–risk decision.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment and your priorities. Surgery or radiotherapy can have a separate role in selected situations. Symptom control, rehabilitation and palliative care can accompany systemic treatment; they are not restricted to the end of life.

items.title: General chemotherapy risks
items.text: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste changes, diarrhoea or constipation; fatigue, hair, nail and skin changes; changes in sexual wellbeing; allergic reactions and intravenous-line complications; blood clots, including clots in the legs or lungs; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, rare later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. The likelihood and severity differ between medicines and people. Use this general discussion together with every medicine-specific risk below.

evidence.title: European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer randomised phase II study: liposomal versus conventional doxorubicin in advanced sarcoma
evidence.summary: A small historical randomised phase II study compared pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² every four weeks with conventional doxorubicin 75 mg/m² every three weeks in advanced sarcoma. Observed response rates were similar, with different toxicity patterns: less severe neutropenia and hair loss but more hand–foot toxicity with the liposomal treatment.
evidence.intro: A small historical randomised phase II study compared pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² every four weeks with conventional doxorubicin 75 mg/m² every three weeks in advanced sarcoma. Observed response rates were similar, with different toxicity patterns: less severe neutropenia and hair loss but more hand–foot toxicity with the liposomal treatment.
evidence.caveat: This was a small phase II trial with an older mixed-sarcoma population, including gastrointestinal stromal tumours. It does not prove modern non-inferiority or a survival advantage, and does not support this chemotherapy as a present-day gastrointestinal stromal tumour recommendation. Breast/ovarian outcomes are separate.
evidence.interpretation: This was a small phase II trial with an older mixed-sarcoma population, including gastrointestinal stromal tumours. questions.a: Treatment aims to control metastatic sarcoma and help symptoms. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² is given on day 1 every 28 days. National Cancer Control Programme describes typically 6 cycles or continuation until progression or unacceptable toxicity; the team confirms duration and review points.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can I restart after a delay or safety hold?
questions.a: Only after the treating team gives an explicit plan. A normal result does not erase a previous severe reaction or permanent-stop decision.

questions.q: Are safety tests the same as checking benefit?
questions.a: No. Safety tests look for treatment effects on the body. Scans, symptoms and function help the specialist assess tumour control.
